CHAPTER.VERS: How beautiful are thy feet with shoes, O prince’s daughter! the joints of thy thighs like jewels, the work of the hands of a skilful workman.

Thy navel a round goblet, wanteth not liquor: thy belly an heap of wheat set about with lilies.
liquor: Heb. mixture
Thy two breasts like two young roes twins.
Thy neck as a tower of ivory; thy eyes the fishpools in Heshbon, by the gate of Bathrabbim: thy nose as the tower of Lebanon which looketh toward Damascus.

Thy head upon thee like Carmel, and the hair of thy head like purple; the king held captive by locks of hair.
Carmel: or, crimson
held: Heb. bound
How fair and how pleasant art thou, O love, for delights!
This thy stature is like a palm tree, and thy breasts to clusters .
I said, I will go up to the palm tree, I will take hold of its boughs: now also thy breasts shall be as clusters of the vine, and the fragrance of thy breath like apples;

And the roof of thy mouth like the best wine for my beloved, that goeth sweetly, causing the lips of those that are asleep to speak.
sweetly: Heb. straightly
of those…: or, of the ancient
I my beloved’s, and his desire toward me.
Come, my beloved, let us go forth into the field; let us lodge in the villages.

Let us get up early to the vineyards; let us see if the vine flourisheth, the tender grape appeareth, the pomegranates bud forth: there will I give thee my loves.
appear: Heb. open
The mandrakes give a fragrance, and at our gates all manner of pleasant , new and old, I have laid up for thee, O my beloved.
